name: Erik Underwood

summary.text: Frank Atwood is chair of the Approval Voting Party and has run for a variety of federal and state offices on the party's line since at least 2014, according to Ballotpedia.

Erik Underwood is chairman of Illmatic Ventures and CEO of the technology companies My24HourNews.com and Vurbil; he has run for office multiple times under different party labels, including Republican (2016, U.S. Senate) and Democratic (2018, governor).

experience.text: Worked in the U.S. Senate in Washington, D.C., and as a student Junior Prosecutor in the Atlanta City Solicitor's Office.
Chairman, Illmatic Ventures; CEO, My24HourNews.com and Vurbil.
Spent roughly eight years litigating a case against Bank of America Corporation in federal court, by his own account.

positions.source_title: End TABOR Once and For All - Erik Underwood for Colorado Governor
positions.quote: I originated the plan in 2018 to eliminate TABOR. It's crippling our state while our infrastructure crumbles. We need to fix our schools, roads, and bridges. No more TABOR workarounds – let's use common sense and get rid of this insanity.
positions.note: Calls for eliminating TABOR outright, which goes further than Proposition NN but is in the same direction (keeping revenue rather than refunding it).

positions.source_title: Healthcare & Human Services - Erik Underwood for Colorado Governor
positions.quote: I will provide all Coloradans with free healthcare, or at minimum $50 maximum per year per family member (with installment plans for lower-income families).
positions.note: Proposes a state universal-healthcare plan funded partly by new payroll and income taxes.

positions.source_title: Environmental Policy - Erik Underwood for Colorado Governor
positions.quote: Accelerate transition to renewables paired with union labor standards and a Just Transition fund for displaced fossil fuel workers in Weld, Garfield, Moffat, and Rio Blanco counties.

positions.source_title: Environmental Policy - Erik Underwood for Colorado Governor
positions.quote: On April 22, 2026, the Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission (ECMC) approved 24 new oil and gas wells at the State Sunlight/Long pad... That decision is wrong, and I opposed it.
positions.note: Inferred disagreement with Amendment 82 from his opposition to new oil and gas development and push to accelerate the renewable transition; the amendment itself (about consumer gas hookups, not drilling) is not addressed directly.

positions.source_title: Youth Violence Policy - Erik Underwood for Colorado Governor
positions.quote: Strengthen safe-storage laws for firearms — most guns used in juvenile shootings in Colorado were stolen from a parent, relative, or unsecured vehicle.
positions.note: Also pledges to 'crack down on ghost guns' and hold straw-purchasers accountable.

positions.source_title: LGBTQ+ Policy - Erik Underwood for Colorado Governor
positions.quote: Protect gender-affirming care for adults and, in consultation with families and medical professionals, for minors — and prosecute any attempt to criminalize physicians, parents, or patients for receiving lawful medical care in Colorado.
positions.note: Opposes restricting gender-affirming care for minors in general terms without specifically addressing surgery, so per the coding guide this is coded no stronger than disagree.

positions.source_title: Justice & Human Rights - Erik Underwood for Colorado Governor
positions.quote: I will sign a bill holding ICE agents accountable for any constitutional or human rights violations in Colorado.
positions.note: Inferred opposition to Amendment 81 from his adversarial stance toward ICE; the amendment's notification requirement is not addressed directly.

research_notes: Underwood has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, but his own campaign site has an unusually detailed set of issue pages for a short-profile candidate, which is why more positions were coded here than the 20-40 minute guideline might otherwise produce; effort was capped once a reasonable set was found rather than mining every page on the site. His campaign's 'Endorsements' page is lorem-ipsum placeholder text with no real content, so endorsements is empty. He ran previously as a Republican (2016, U.S. Senate) and a Democrat (2018, governor); this history is neutral biographical fact from Ballotpedia, not characterization. His current 2026 campaign finance totals were not found; the only figure on Ballotpedia ($22,488 raised) is from a disqualified 2020 Senate primary and is not reported here as current.
